units.function: Pure resolver that parses Agent, Project, Issue and Run trust policy JSON, selects standard versus low-trust-review execution, intersects low-trust boundaries and rejects unsupported, invalid, cross-Company, conflicting-root or unscoped policies.
units.dependencyDirection: The resolver depends only on shared Zod schemas/constants and is consumed by AuthorizationService and runtime/workspace flows. Persistence rows are projected into a small input shape before evaluation, making this one of the cleaner policy components.
units.keyDataModels: TrustPreset, four ordered policy sources, LowTrustBoundary with Company/project/root Issue/Issue/Agent/Secret binding/tool class/output promotion constraints, structured denied resolution and source-presets provenance.
units.lifecycle: Each source is parsed from top-level and nested authorization policy fields; any low-trust implication makes the effective preset low trust. Source Company IDs must match. List constraints are normalized and intersected, root Issue IDs must agree, and a concrete project/root/Issue scope is mandatory before returning a low-trust boundary.
units.testAssessment: Six focused pure tests cover default standard, three-source intersection, unknown preset, missing concrete scope, cross-Company source/boundary and normalization preservation. Missing are Run source, invalid authorization/boundary shapes, conflicting root IDs, empty set intersections, duplicate/order normalization, allowed Secret/tool/Agent constraints independently, output-promotion conflicts and mixed top-level/nested declarations. The implementation silently prefers topPreset/topReviewPreset/authPreset/authReviewPreset in that order, so an explicit top-level standard can mask a nested low-trust preset instead of rejecting ambiguity. Non-object raw policy becomes absent/standard. outputPromotionTarget is last-non-null-wins rather than intersected or conflict-checked. Multi-dimensional boundary matching is OR-based downstream, leaving conjunction semantics under-specified.
units.designRationale: Fail closed when a restricted execution policy cannot be understood, and combine restrictions from increasingly specific Agent/Project/Issue/Run contexts so no source can simply widen enumerated allowlists.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a pure, deterministic PolicyContext compiler that combines organization, Work, data, risk, approval and runtime restrictions with explicit precedence and a reproducible policy digest.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the pure discriminated result, source provenance, strict parsing, cross-tenant rejection, restrictive-set intersection and mandatory concrete scope. Replace positional field precedence with one canonical schema or conflict rejection, define conjunction/union semantics per dimension, conflict-check scalar constraints, include policy/schema version and canonical digest, and extend sources to ResponsibilityContract, DataAuthorization, Approval and Connector attestation. Keep it independent from persistence and HTTP.
units.responsibilityConflict: The resolver has no accountable-human, ResponsibilityContract, approval, action digest, data purpose/export or effective-time inputs. A low-trust boundary can therefore constrain technical resources without proving who accepted responsibility. Ambiguous duplicate preset fields and last-writer scalar promotion policy can produce an effective authorization context that no single human explicitly approved.

units.function: Pure unit tests for trust-preset defaulting, restrictive boundary intersection, fail-closed parsing/scoping, Company isolation and JSON normalization preservation.
units.dependencyDirection: Tests call the resolver directly with shared policy schemas and also verify Issue execution-policy normalization, crossing the boundary between trust resolution and serialization compatibility without database or runtime dependencies.
units.keyDataModels: Agent/Project/Issue policy inputs, low-trust boundary dimensions, standard/low-trust/denied results, review preset version and raw-output disposition.
units.lifecycle: Construct policies, resolve once and assert exact effective boundary or denial; one case normalizes policy JSON and confirms custom extension data survives serialization.
units.testAssessment: ADAPT as a concise base suite, then add a generated pairwise source/dimension matrix, malformed scalar/object inputs, contradictory duplicate preset declarations, Run policy, scalar conflict rules, empty intersections, output promotion, stable digest/provenance and property-based tests proving that adding a restriction can never widen the effective set.
units.designRationale: Prove the safety-critical property that low-trust selection and boundary composition fail closed while allowing extension fields to round-trip.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs monotonic policy-composition tests: every more restrictive source must preserve or narrow authority, never widen it accidentally.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the small table-driven style and add monotonicity/property tests against the Company OS PolicyContext compiler and canonical serializer.
units.responsibilityConflict: Tests validate technical resource boundaries only; they do not bind policies to an accountable human, accepted responsibility, approval evidence or exact Work/action snapshot.
